apocryphal._note: Every proper personal name attested in the fetched public-domain English translations of the Gospel of Thomas, Gospel of Philip, Gospel of Mary, and Protevangelium of James (see text_sources), tagged canonical-overlap / palestinian-typical / atypical. Counts are exact mechanical concordance counts (see method), not estimates.

entries.name: Jesus
entries.note: Speaker attribution ("Jesus said") opens nearly every one of the 114 sayings.

entries.name: Thomas
entries.note: Incipit ("...Didymos Judas Thomas wrote them down") and saying 13 (addressed by name, twice more).

entries.name: Simon
entries.note: As "Simon Peter," sayings 13 and 114.

entries.name: Peter
entries.note: As "Simon Peter," sayings 13 and 114.

entries.name: Matthew
entries.note: Saying 13.

entries.name: Mary
entries.note: Sayings 21 and 114; usually read as Mary Magdalene, text does not disambiguate.

entries.name: Salome
entries.note: Saying 61 (dialogue with Jesus at her couch); the name is used once, as speaker attribution.

entries.name: James
entries.note: Saying 12, "James the righteous" (James the Just, brother of Jesus).

entries.name: Adam
entries.note: Sayings 46 and 85; OT figure, also named in the canonical genealogy at Luke 3:38.

entries.name: John
entries.note: Saying 46, all three occurrences "John the Baptist" ("from Adam until John the Baptist... no one so superior to John the Baptist... will become superior to John").

entries.name: Didymos
entries.note: Incipit, "Didymos Judas Thomas" (Didymos = "twin"); the same epithet is used for Thomas at John 11:16, 20:24, 21:2 ("Thomas, called Didymus").

entries.name: Judas
entries.note: Incipit, "Didymos Judas Thomas" — Thomas's given name in this text's attribution.

entries.name: Caesar
entries.note: Saying 100 ("Give Caesar what belongs to Caesar..."); parallels Matt 22:21, Mark 12:17, Luke 20:25.

entries.name: Jesus
entries.note: Personal name "Jesus" as distinct from the title "Christ" (titles excluded from this count).

entries.name: Mary
entries.note: Mother of Jesus and/or Mary Magdalene, including the "three Marys" passage (mother / sister / companion, all named Mary).

entries.name: Magdalene
entries.note: As "Mary Magdalene," named as the Savior's companion, kissed by him "more than the rest of the disciples."

entries.name: Levi
entries.note: Cited in a maxim about worldly possessions; Levi the tax collector is named at Mark 2:14/Luke 5:27.

entries.name: Philip
entries.note: "Philip the apostle said, Joseph the carpenter planted a garden..." — the apostle appears once inside the text that bears his name.

entries.name: Joseph
entries.note: "Joseph the carpenter," father figure of Jesus, discussed re: the wood of the cross.

entries.name: Adam
entries.note: Central to the text's creation discourse; OT figure also named in Luke 3:38.

entries.name: Eve
entries.note: Paired with Adam in the creation discourse; not named in the four canonical Gospels/Acts (cf. Paul, 2 Cor 11:3), and not a name attested for living women in Tal Ilan's Palestinian corpus — treated as mythic/symbolic here.

entries.name: Abraham
entries.note: Discussed re: circumcision as a "sign"; also named repeatedly in the canonical Gospels (e.g. Matt 1, John 8).

entries.name: Sophia
entries.note: Valentinian Gnostic personification of Wisdom, treated in the text almost as a character; Greek theological/philosophical name, not a Palestinian Jewish personal name.

entries.name: Echamoth
entries.note: Wordplay pair on "Wisdom"/"Wisdom of death" used as quasi-personal names for the lower and upper Sophia; Coptic-Gnostic coinage, not a real attested name.

entries.name: Echmoth
entries.note: Wordplay pair on "Wisdom"/"Wisdom of death" used as quasi-personal names for the lower and upper Sophia; Coptic-Gnostic coinage, not a real attested name.

entries.name: Mary
entries.note: Protagonist, generally identified as Mary Magdalene, though the extant fragment itself never uses the word "Magdalene."

entries.name: Levi
entries.note: Levi the tax collector, identified with Matthew at Mark 2:14/Luke 5:27.

entries.name: Joachim
entries.note: Father of Mary; Hebrew name (form of Jehoiachin/Eliakim), well attested in the period though not a canonical-Gospel character.

entries.name: Anna
entries.note: Mother of Mary; same name as the prophetess Anna of Luke 2:36-38 (a distinct person, but the same name — like this text's Salome — so counted as overlap).

entries.name: Zacharias
entries.note: Priest, father of John the Baptist; martyred in the temple in this text's expanded legend.

entries.name: John
entries.note: The infant John the Baptist, hidden with Elizabeth from Herod's soldiers.

entries.name: Salome
entries.note: The skeptical midwife who tests Mary's virginity; same name as the canonical disciple/daughter of Herodias, but a distinct character here.

entries.name: James
entries.note: Narrator ("I, James, wrote this history..."), presented as Joseph's son, i.e. James the Just / brother of the Lord.

entries.name: Rubim
entries.note: Rebukes Joachim for offering first, and is named again in Anna's song ("the sons of Rubim"); this translation's spelling of the name given as "Reuben"/"Reubel" in others — an attested patriarchal Hebrew name.

entries.name: Simeon
entries.note: Priest chosen by lot after Zacharias's death, told he would not see death until he had seen the Messiah — the same figure and role as Luke 2's Simeon.

entries.name: Annas
entries.note: "Annas the scribe," a minor character who reports Zacharias's absence; same name as the high priest Annas of Luke 3:2/John 18/Acts 4.

entries.name: Jesus
entries.note: The text's own title, two annunciation formulas ("you shall call His name Jesus"), and the closing doxology.

entries.name: Isaac
entries.note: Named in Joachim's genealogical lament and Anna's prayer; also named in the canonical genealogies (Matt 1:2, Luke 3:34).

entries.name: Jacob
entries.note: Named alongside Isaac in Salome's prayer; also named in the canonical genealogies (Matt 1:2, Luke 3:34) and at John 4:5.

entries.name: Samuel
entries.note: A priest who serves in Zacharias's place while he is mute; distinct from the prophet Samuel, but the same name — which is itself named at Acts 3:24 and 13:20 (excludes a second raw match that was the inline citation "1 Samuel 1:11," not a character).

entries.name: David
entries.note: "The family of David" — Mary and Joseph's Davidic descent; also named in the canonical genealogies (Matt 1, Luke 3) and elsewhere.

entries.name: Augustus
entries.note: The census decree; parallels Luke 2:1 ("a decree from Caesar Augustus").

entries.name: Gabriel
entries.note: The "archangel Gabriel" who spoke to Mary; named at Luke 1:19, 26.

entries.name: Sarah
entries.note: Invoked in Anna's prayer ("as You blessed the womb of Sarah"); OT matriarch, not named in the four Gospels/Acts.

entries.name: Judith
entries.note: Anna's maidservant, a minor named character; attested Jewish woman's name of the period.

entries.name: Dathan
entries.note: Cited by the priest as a warning to Joseph ("remember what the Lord did to Dathan, and Abiram, and Korah," Numbers 16); a pre-monarchic wilderness-era name, not typical of Ilan's Roman-period Palestinian corpus.

entries.name: Abiram
entries.note: See Dathan — same citation (Numbers 16).

entries.name: Korah
entries.note: See Dathan — same citation (Numbers 16).

Gospel of Thomas.date_of_text: 2nd century (c. 100-150 CE; possibly incorporates earlier independent sayings tradition)

apocryphal.method: A CI job (scripts/fetch-sources.mjs + scripts/extract-apocrypha-names.mjs) fetched each translation, stripped HTML, and mechanically counted a broad candidate list of biblical/early-Christian personal names plus flagged other capitalized non-sentence-initial words for review (data/fetched/apocrypha-names.json). Those raw whole-page counts were then reviewed by hand against a full-text diagnostic dump printed to the CI job log (never committed) to exclude: (1) site chrome — navigation menus, translator bylines, and funder/copyright footers that happen to repeat a candidate name (e.g. translator "Thomas O. Lambdin," or a "Gospel of Mary" page's large pre-text book-recommendation sidebar, which alone accounted for nearly all of that page's raw Mary/Magdalene/Jesus/John/Sophia matches); and (2) inline scripture cross-reference citations New Advent adds to the Protevangelium (e.g. "Matthew 1:19," "1 Samuel 1:11") which cite a book, not a character. The counts above are of the real body text only (title through closing doxology/final saying). Titles (Christ, Lord, Savior, Father, God) are excluded throughout. Tagging: canonical-overlap = the same name (not necessarily the same individual — e.g. this text's Salome, Anna, and Samuel are each a different person from their canonical namesake, but the rule counts the NAME) appears in the four canonical Gospels or Acts; palestinian-typical = not a canonical name, but common in Tal Ilan's Palestine 330 BCE-200 CE lexicon; atypical = Gnostic/theological coinages, mythic figures, or pre-monarchic OT names not typical of that Roman-period corpus.
apocryphal.build_note: Fetched in CI 2026-09-26 via scripts/fetch-sources.mjs (all four first-choice URLs succeeded; see data/fetched/apocrypha-names.json for fetch_date/translation per text). Rebuilt locally from the attested counts, with corrections: dropped Gospel of Mary's "Jesus" entry (0 real attestations — the extant fragment, Chapter 4 to the end of Chapter 9, never once uses the personal name, calling him only "the Savior"/"the Lord"); renamed "Reuben / Reubel" to "Rubim" (the spelling this translation actually uses); split "Simon Peter" into separate Simon/Peter entries and "John the Baptist" into a plain "John" entry to match the candidate-name schema; added newly-discovered attested names found via the capitalized-word review list: Didymos, Judas, Caesar (Thomas); Levi, Magdalene (Philip, split out from the old combined "Mary Magdalene" entry); Isaac, Jacob, Samuel, David, Augustus, Gabriel, Sarah, Judith, Dathan, Abiram, Korah (Protevangelium). Also retagged Anna from palestinian-typical to canonical-overlap (Luke 2:36's prophetess Anna is a different person but the same name, matching how this file already treats this text's Salome).
